target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams using many cloud apps
problem: Work files and actions are scattered across many cloud apps; Slapdash gave a keyboard-driven command bar and unified search across them.
business_model: SaaS subscription, 12 dollars per month paid plan plus enterprise tier at 2021 launch

founders.name: Ivan Kanevski
prior_employers: Facebook (nearly six years as software engineer)
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as engineer and designer.

founders.name: Dmitry Koterov
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Low-latency file system, indexing of 40 plus apps via integrations and cross platform clients is substantial for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations took effort but platform owners and search players could replicate; no data moat evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ClickUp bought Slapdash as its first acquisition on 2022-04-26 and sunset the standalone product.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported demand for fast navigation across tools, citing Superhuman as inspiration, but no dated spend data was found.

branding.name_origin: Product term Command Bar is a blend of command line and search bar per Slapdash docs; origin of the company name not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable word but implies carelessness; no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Slapdash raised a 3.7M seed in March 2021 and was bought by ClickUp in April 2022, its first acquisition, with the founders joining ClickUp. The standalone product was closed and rebuilt into ClickUp search, so the outcome reads as a small strategic acquisition about a year after seed; terms were not disclosed.
notes: Sources disagree on founding year (2018 or 2019). The Cerv Ventures page also reports the seed. The slapdash.com site now shows a sunset notice pointing users to ClickUp. No dated competitor source found near the batch (Command-E, Alfred and Spotlight are undated), so the list is empty.
